SOURCE: https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/optimizations/spark-ui-guide/long-spark-stage-page
FETCHED: 2026-06-17
PART OF: Spark UI Guide series (Step 3 of 5)

=== SPILL ===
"The first thing to look for in a long-running stage is whether there's spill."
"Spill is what happens when Spark runs low on memory. It starts to move data from memory to disk, and this can be quite expensive."
Check stage page top for spill statistics.
No spill stats shown → no spill.
Spill stats shown → consult shuffle/spill optimization guidance.

=== SKEW ===
"The next thing we want to look into is whether there's skew."
"Skew is when one or just a few tasks take much longer than the rest."
Navigate to Summary Metrics.
Compare Max duration vs 75th percentile duration.
"If the Max duration is 50% more than the 75th percentile, you may be suffering from skew."
Equal values → healthy.

=== NO SKEW / NO SPILL PATH ===
Return to job page → scroll to top → click "Associated Job Ids"
→ leads to Spark stage high I/O troubleshooting (Step 4)
